- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) or negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 20–40% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00 or 0.67 followed by 0.33), model often overshoots; apply a 10–30% downward correction to the peak forecast.
- If sentiment history shows prolonged bullish (≥0.67) but prices are trending down, model overreacts; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 10–25% from forecast if 3–5 days of high sentiment precede a drop.
- For 30d forecasts, if model shows >5x the recent 18d average or >3x the 18d median, flag as overconfident and scale down by 30–50%.
- When sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33/0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 18d average as baseline and adjust forecast ±10% based on sentiment direction.
- If sentiment is 0.00 or negative, model often ignores risk; apply a hard floor at 0.05–0.10 for 30d forecast to prevent negative drift.
